```{r}
#| label: setup
here::i_am("reports/analysis_report.qmd")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
)

comp <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/05_missing_value_methods.rds"))
da   <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/06_differential_abundance.rds"))
res  <- readr::read_csv(here::here("results/differential_abundance.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

tier_cols <- c("barrier-robust"  = "#eb6834",
               "main model only" = "#2a78d6",
               "not significant" = "grey75")
```

## Handling of missing values

Missing values are more frequent in controls than in AD after adjusting for
batch and age (see QC report), so their treatment can bias the AD vs. control
comparison. Three treatments were compared on the same model
(`~ group + batch + age + sex`): limma on observed values only, limma after
left-censored imputation (down-shifted normal, 1.8 SD shift, 0.3 SD width), and
proDA, which models the probability of a value being missing as a function of
intensity without imputing.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-method-direction
#| tbl-cap: "Protein groups with FDR < 5% by method and direction of change."
long <- comp |>
  pivot_longer(-c(protein, gene, missing_control, missing_AD),
               names_to = c(".value", "method"),
               names_pattern = "(logFC|p_adj|p)_(observed|imputed|proda)")

long |>
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) |>
  count(method, direction = if_else(logFC > 0, "higher in AD", "lower in AD")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(total = `higher in AD` + `lower in AD`) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-method-agreement
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement of each alternative with proDA (FDR < 5%)."
agreement <- function(alt) {
  sig_p <- comp$p_adj_proda < 0.05
  sig_a <- comp[[paste0("p_adj_", alt)]] < 0.05
  tibble(method = alt,
         both = sum(sig_p & sig_a, na.rm = TRUE),
         `proDA only` = sum(sig_p & !sig_a, na.rm = TRUE),
         `alternative only` = sum(!sig_p & sig_a, na.rm = TRUE))
}
bind_rows(agreement("observed"), agreement("imputed")) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-method-logfc
#| fig-cap: "AD vs control log2 fold change of each alternative against proDA. Each point is a protein group; colour is the difference in missing-value fraction between controls and AD. Dashed line: identity."
#| fig-width: 8
comp |>
  mutate(missing_gap = missing_control - missing_AD) |>
  pivot_longer(c(logFC_observed, logFC_imputed),
               names_to = "method", values_to = "logFC_alt") |>
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         logFC_observed = "Observed values only",
                         logFC_imputed  = "Left-censored imputation")) |>
  ggplot(aes(logFC_proda, logFC_alt, colour = missing_gap)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = ~ filter(.x, gene %in% c("NEFL", "UCHL1")),
            aes(label = gene), colour = "black", vjust = -0.8, size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ method) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "grey85", high = "#eb6834",
                         midpoint = 0,
                         name = "Missing fraction\ncontrols − AD") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change, proDA", y = "log2 fold change, alternative")
```

Left-censored imputation inflates effect sizes across the proteome, most
strongly for protein groups with more missing values in controls, and changes
the set of significant protein groups substantially. Limma on observed values
agrees closely with proDA; discordant protein groups lie near the FDR
threshold with near-identical fold changes. proDA is used for the main
analysis; limma on observed values with sample quality weights is reported as
a sensitivity analysis.

## Differential abundance

Main model: proDA, `r da$model`, AD vs control, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Site
(rather than MS batch) is used because each site was measured in a single batch
and site separates Kiel (controls only) from Magdeburg.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-da-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Protein groups by result tier and direction of change."
res |>
  count(tier, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Volcano plot, AD vs control (main model). Barrier-robust protein groups remain significant after adjusting for the plasma-protein score. Adjusted p-values below 1e-16 are shown at 1e-16."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5
label_genes <- c("MAPT", "SOD1", "PARK7", "UCHL1", "NEFL", "SMOC1", "YWHAZ",
                 "ALDOA", "SPP1", "PKM", "ENO2", "FABP3")
res |>
  mutate(neglog_p = -log10(pmax(p_adj, 1e-16)),
         tier = factor(tier, levels = names(tier_cols))) |>
  ggplot(aes(log2FC, neglog_p, colour = tier)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = ~ filter(.x, gene %in% label_genes) |> distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE),
            aes(label = gene), colour = "black", size = 3, vjust = -0.7,
            check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = tier_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change, AD vs control", y = "−log10 adjusted p-value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Positive controls

```{r}
#| label: tbl-controls
#| tbl-cap: "Known CSF markers of AD. MAPT is partly circular, since diagnosis is defined from CSF tau."
res |>
  filter(gene %in% c("MAPT", "SOD1", "PARK7", "UCHL1", "NEFL")) |>
  transmute(gene, tier, log2FC = round(log2FC, 2),
            p_adj = signif(pmax(p_adj, 1e-16), 2),
            p_adj_plasma_adjusted = signif(p_adj_plasma_adjusted, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

### Sensitivity analyses

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement of each sensitivity analysis with the main model: correlation of log2 fold changes, and significant protein groups shared, lost and gained."
da$sensitivity_summary |>
  mutate(r_logFC = round(r_logFC, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Results are unchanged without the runs flagged for blood contamination and
after renormalization (the renormalized list differs only near the FDR
threshold, as all fold changes shift by the small diagnosis-associated offset
seen in QC). Limma with sample weights recovers the same effects with more
power. Adjusting for the plasma-protein score, which is lower in AD, reduces
the significant set to a core of protein groups. Whether the score acts as a
confounder (barrier permeability) or a mediator of disease effects cannot be
resolved without the CSF/serum albumin quotient, which is not available; both
tiers are therefore reported.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tier-direction
#| tbl-cap: "Direction of change by tier. Decreases in AD depend more on the plasma-protein balance than increases."
res |>
  filter(tier != "not significant") |>
  count(tier, direction) |>
  group_by(tier) |>
  mutate(`% of tier` = round(100 * n / sum(n))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Of the 67 protein groups lower in AD, 61 lose significance after the plasma
adjustment, whereas most of those higher in AD remain. Lower levels in AD are
largely explained by the plasma-protein balance; the most specific signal is
the release of brain-derived proteins.

### Barrier-robust core

```{r}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Barrier-robust protein groups: z-scored log2 intensities per run (grey: missing), runs ordered by diagnosis and site, protein groups ordered by log2 fold change."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
filt <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/04_filter.rds"))
keep <- !filt$sample$excluded
core <- filter(res, tier == "barrier-robust") |> arrange(log2FC)

Z <- log2(filt$intensity[core$protein_group, keep])
Z <- t(scale(t(Z)))
smp_order <- filt$sample[keep, ] |> arrange(group, site) |> pull(run)

as_tibble(Z, rownames = "protein_group") |>
  left_join(select(core, protein_group, gene), by = "protein_group") |>
  pivot_longer(-c(protein_group, gene), names_to = "run", values_to = "z") |>
  left_join(select(filt$sample, run, group), by = "run") |>
  mutate(run  = factor(run, levels = smp_order),
         gene = factor(protein_group, levels = core$protein_group,
                       labels = make.unique(core$gene))) |>
  ggplot(aes(run, gene, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(~ group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "white", high = "#eb6834",
                       limits = c(-3, 3), oob = scales::squish, na.value = "grey85",
                       name = "z-score") +
  labs(x = "Runs", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

The core is dominated by glycolytic enzymes (ALDOA, ALDOC, PKM, LDHA, GPI,
ENO2, PGK1), 14-3-3 proteins (YWHAZ, YWHAG, YWHAE) and established CSF markers
of AD (MAPT, SOD1, UCHL1, SMOC1, SPP1, FABP3), mostly intracellular proteins
higher in AD. The glycolytic signature replicates the original report.

## Diagnostic classifier

An elastic-net logistic regression (α = 0.5, penalty chosen by inner 5-fold
cross-validation, `lambda.1se`) classifies AD vs control from the proteome.
Protein selection, imputation of missing values (half the training minimum)
and scaling are learned within each training split. MAPT is excluded, as
diagnosis is defined from CSF tau, and Kiel is excluded, as its controls are
age-mismatched and include no AD. Performance is estimated by 10 × 5-fold
nested cross-validation and by leave-one-site-out validation, against an
age + sex baseline.

```{r}
#| label: clf-load
clf <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/08_classifier.rds"))

roc_df <- function(y, prob) {
  r <- pROC::roc(y, prob, direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  tibble(fpr = 1 - r$specificities, tpr = r$sensitivities) |> arrange(fpr, tpr)
}
```

`r clf$params$n_features` protein groups with ≤ `r 100 * clf$params$max_missing`%
missing values were candidate predictors.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-clf-auc
#| tbl-cap: "Area under the ROC curve: nested cross-validation (mean and range over 10 repetitions) and leave-one-site-out validation."
cv_row <- clf$cv_auc |>
  summarise(validation   = "Nested CV (10 × 5-fold)",
            n            = nrow(filter(clf$cv_pred, repetition == 1)),
            auc_proteome = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", mean(auc_proteome),
                                   min(auc_proteome), max(auc_proteome)),
            auc_baseline = sprintf("%.2f", mean(auc_baseline)))
site_rows <- clf$loso_auc |>
  transmute(validation   = paste("Held-out site:", site),
            n,
            auc_proteome = sprintf("%.2f", auc_proteome),
            auc_baseline = sprintf("%.2f", auc_baseline))
bind_rows(cv_row, site_rows) |>
  rename(`AUC proteome` = auc_proteome, `AUC age + sex` = auc_baseline) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-roc
#| fig-cap: "ROC curves. Left: nested cross-validation, one line per repetition (proteome) and age + sex baseline. Right: leave-one-site-out, one line per held-out site."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
cv_curves <- clf$cv_pred |>
  group_by(repetition) |>
  group_modify(~ bind_rows(
    mutate(roc_df(.x$y, .x$prob), model = "Proteome"),
    mutate(roc_df(.x$y, .x$prob_baseline), model = "Age + sex")
  )) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(panel = "Nested cross-validation", line = paste(model, repetition))

site_curves <- clf$loso |>
  group_by(site) |>
  group_modify(~ roc_df(.x$y, .x$prob)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(panel = "Leave-one-site-out", model = site, line = site)

roc_cols <- c("Proteome" = "#eb6834", "Age + sex" = "grey60",
              "Berlin" = "#2a78d6", "Magdeburg" = "#eb6834", "Sweden" = "#1baf7a")

bind_rows(cv_curves, site_curves) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Nested cross-validation", "Leave-one-site-out"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(fpr, tpr, group = line, colour = model)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey75") +
  geom_step(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = roc_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "1 − specificity", y = "Sensitivity") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-selection
#| fig-cap: "Selection stability: fraction of the 50 outer-fold models selecting each protein group (top 20). Colour: sign of the mean coefficient."
#| fig-height: 5
clf$selection |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  mutate(label = make.unique(gene),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(label)),
         sign  = if_else(mean_coef > 0, "higher in AD", "lower in AD")) |>
  ggplot(aes(freq, label, fill = sign)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("higher in AD" = "#eb6834", "lower in AD" = "#2a78d6"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Selected in outer-fold models", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The proteome discriminates AD from controls well beyond age and sex. Performance
is maintained on held-out Swedish and Magdeburg cohorts and lower on Berlin,
the largest cohort (so the model is trained on fewer samples when it is held
out), whose biochemical controls are mostly patients with other clinical
diagnoses. The most stable predictors (14-3-3 proteins, glycolytic enzymes,
SPP1, SMOC1) coincide with the barrier-robust core of the differential
abundance analysis, although the classifier did not use those results.
Because diagnosis is defined biochemically from tau and Aβ, residual
circularity through tau-correlated proteins cannot be excluded.
